course_name_original: Ciencia y tecnología de los materiales
prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed, or at least be currently studying, the subjects from the previous year.

learning_outcomes.text: Understands the fundamental concepts of bonding, structure, and microstructure of different types of materials
Understands the relationship between the material's microstructure and its mechanical, electrical, thermal, and magnetic behavior
Understands the mechanical behavior of metallic, ceramic, plastic, and composite materials
Knows how properties can be modified through mechanical processes and heat treatments
Knows the basic techniques for structural characterization of materials
Acquires skills in handling diagrams and graphs
Analyzes the obtained results and draws conclusions from them
Is able to apply material testing standards

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Materials Science and Technology. Classification of materials. Terminology. Guidelines for following the course.
Crystalline and amorphous solids. Crystal lattices, characteristics, and imperfections. Allotropic transformations.

Mechanical, chemical, thermal, electrical, and magnetic properties. Material testing standards. Tensile and compressive behavior. Fundamentals of fracture. Toughness. Concept of hardness in engineering. Main testing methods. Introduction to Metallography. Monophasic and biphasic structures. Matrix constituent and dispersed constituents. Formulation, proposal, and resolution of exercises and/or practical cases related to each test.

Solidification. Constitution of alloys. Grain size. Main binary equilibrium diagrams. Processing. Carbon steels and cast irons: Classification and applications. Heat treatments: Objectives, fundamentals, and classification. Annealing, normalizing, quenching, and tempering. Non-ferrous alloys.
Classification based on molecular structure: Thermoplastics, thermosets, and elastomers. Properties and evaluation methods. Shaping processes. Introduction to Composite Materials.
Classification and properties. Traditional glasses and ceramics. Technological ceramics. Cements: phases, types, and main applications. Concrete. Processing of ceramic materials.

assessment_methods.method: Practice reports, attendance, and participation in practices
Oral presentation and defense of group work
Partial I exam on theoretical content (objective questions)
Partial II exam on theoretical content (objective questions)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment in the 1st edition, the sum of scores must reach a minimum of 5 out of 10, and a minimum of 40% (1.2 points) in Partial I and 40% (1.6 points) in Partial II is required. Alternatively, a minimum of 45% (3.15 points over 7) can be achieved considering both partials jointly. For continuous assessment in the 2nd edition, the sum of scores must reach a minimum of 5 out of 10, and a minimum of 45% (3.15 points over 7) in the single theoretical exam (70% weight) is required, while practical test scores (30% weight) are retained. If minimums are not met, the maximum grade recorded is 4.5. Global assessment in both editions and the extraordinary call consists of a single written exam (100% weight) covering all theoretical and practical content, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10. Students are expected to demonstrate appropriate ethical behavior, as detailed in the University of Vigo's regulations.
